qt: to the Commission Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew) Subject:

In a recent interview with the Financial Times1, the Taliban regime’s de facto Foreign Minister reportedly expressed the hope that EU-hosted talks with Taliban representatives in June 2026 would lead to the easing or lifting of sanctions, which he claimed had failed to achieve their intended objectives. In its reply to Written Question P-002653/20262, the Commission stated that the discussions were strictly limited to procedural steps concerning the readmission of Afghan nationals and noted that consular services fall within the competence of the Member States. However, decisions concerning EU restrictive measures and sanctions relief fall within EU competence. In the light of this: 1.

Had the Taliban indicated prior to the June meeting that sanctions relief, economic support or other forms of economic concessions were among its expectations or requests in connection with cooperation on the return and readmission of Afghan nationals?

Can the Commission confirm that, at no point during the June meeting, were the easing or lifting of EU restrictive measures, sanctions relief, or any other form of economic support or benefit for the Taliban discussed, either formally or informally?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.10.2026) The Commission refers the Honourable Member to the reply to written question P002653/261. Following a letter signed by 20 Member States and Schengen Associated countries dated 16 October 2025, the Commission and Sweden, on behalf of the Member States, co-chaired a technical-level meeting in Brussels with representatives of the de facto authorities of Afghanistan responsible for return and readmission, in particular with regards to the identification of returnees, the issuance of travel documents and their return. The technical meeting was dedicated strictly on return and readmission focusing on criminals and persons who pose a threat to public order and national security. Principled operational technical-level engagement with the de facto authorities of Afghanistan is in line with the Council conclusions of September 20212 and March 20233.
